# last change in code by Martin Safranek (2026-07-19).
from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.io import StrInput, Output
from lfx.schema.dataframe import DataFrame

import pandas as pd
import json


class APIPipelineInput(Component):
    display_name = "API Pipeline Input"
    description = "Reads pipeline_input from API or from manual UI JSON and outputs a single-row DataFrame."

    inputs = [
        # this is the API entry point
        StrInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="API input (JSON string)",
            required=False
        ),

        # only for UI testing
        StrInput(
            name="manual_json",
            display_name="Manual JSON (UI testing only)",
            required=False
        )
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(
            name="result",
            display_name="Pipeline DataFrame",
            method="process",
            type=DataFrame
        )
    ]

    def process(self) -> DataFrame:

        raw = None

        # -------- API call path --------
        if self.input_value:
            raw = self.input_value

        # -------- UI manual fallback --------
        elif self.manual_json:
            raw = self.manual_json

        if not raw:
            raise ValueError("No input provided (API input_value nor manual JSON).")

        try:
            data = json.loads(raw)
        except Exception as e:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid JSON input: {e}")

        if "pipeline_input" not in data:
            raise ValueError("Missing 'pipeline_input' in JSON")

        if not isinstance(data["pipeline_input"], dict):
            raise ValueError("'pipeline_input' must be an object")

        df = pd.DataFrame([data["pipeline_input"]])

        # Preserve original file name (without UUID prefix) for deduplication
        if "file_name" in df.columns:
            import re
            raw_name = str(df["file_name"].iloc[0]) if not df.empty else ""
            # Strip UUID prefix: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx_
            clean_name = re.sub(r'^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}_', '', raw_name)
            df["original_file_name"] = clean_name

        return DataFrame(df)

# last change in code by Jan Drozd (2026-08-20).
from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.io import DataFrameInput, StrInput, SecretStrInput, Output
from lfx.schema.dataframe import DataFrame

import os
import csv
import io
import re
import json
import uuid
import logging
import unicodedata
from eduai_normalize import detect_lang
import pandas as pd

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# is_active is how a CSV row asks to be REMOVED, so the spellings a spreadsheet
# actually produces all have to land: Czech Excel writes PRAVDA/NEPRAVDA, an
# English one TRUE/FALSE, a formula 1/0. Anything unrecognised RAISES rather
# than defaulting — guessing here either resurrects a deleted answer or deletes
# a live one, and both are silent.
_TRUEISH = {"", "true", "1", "t", "y", "yes", "ano", "a", "pravda"}
_FALSEISH = {"false", "0", "f", "n", "no", "ne", "nepravda"}


def _slug(text: str, taken: set) -> str:
    """A stable, readable entry_key derived from the question.

    Only used when the CSV leaves entry_key empty, i.e. for a row a human just
    typed. Deriving from the QUESTION is safe in a way the old pack_id
    derivation was not: that one derived from METADATA
    (`language-subject-grade`), which was identical for different content and so
    made two packs overwrite each other. Two identical questions in one pack is
    already a reported error (qa_duplicate_questions, migration 142), and the
    `-2` suffix below keeps even that case from colliding.
    """
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", (text or "").lower())
    s = "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s).strip("-")[:48] or "entry"
    cand, n = s, 2
    while cand in taken:
        cand = f"{s}-{n}"
        n += 1
    taken.add(cand)
    return cand


# pack_id is the REPLACEMENT KEY (uploading the same name replaces that pack's
# previous version), so it must be a stable, typable identifier — never derived.
# Derivation used to build `lang-subject-grade`, which gave every plain upload
# "cs-core" and made the second upload silently replace the first.
_PACK_ID_RX = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")


def _asset_refs_json(cell: str):
    """The entry's CITED SOURCES â€” one per LINE in the CSV cell â€” as a JSON
    string, or None. A line is `Titulek | https://â€¦`; the title may be omitted
    and the URL then stands in for it, which is how RagSource already titles a
    web page. Stored shape is [{"title": â€¦, "url": â€¦}], i.e. the subset of
    RagSource every client renders, so the search side can hand it to `sources`
    without a second mapping.

    A line with no URL is kept as a title-only source (a paper document the
    school hands out has no link), but a line whose URL is not http(s) is
    dropped: web_chat refuses to linkify it anyway, and a `javascript:` href in
    a curated answer is not something to pass through.
    """
    if not cell:
        return None
    out, seen = [], set()
    for line in str(cell).splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        title, sep, url = s.partition("|")
        title, url = title.strip(), url.strip()
        if not sep:                      # a bare line: URL if it looks like one
            title, url = ("", title) if title.lower().startswith(
                ("http://", "https://")) else (title, "")
            # ...and a bare line carrying ANY other scheme is a botched link,
            # not a title. Keeping it would print `javascript:alert(1)` under
            # "Zdroje" as though the school had cited it.
            if title and re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.\-]*:", title):
                continue
        if url and not url.lower().startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            continue
        key = (url or title).lower()
        if not key or key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        out.append({"title": title or url, "url": url or None})
    return json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False) if out else None


def _curated_variants_json(cell: str):
    """The entry's own alternative phrasings — one per LINE in the CSV cell —
    as a JSON string, or None. Empty and duplicate lines are dropped. The
    canonical question is NOT included: the exploder emits it first on its
    own. Excel/Sheets wraps a multi-line cell in quotes automatically, which
    the csv module then un-wraps back to real newlines."""
    if not cell:
        return None
    out, seen = [], set()
    for line in str(cell).splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if s and s.lower() not in seen:
            seen.add(s.lower())
            out.append(s)
    return json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False) if out else None


class QAJsonReader(Component):
    """Reads a QA CSV file (path taken from the API pipeline row) → MULTI-row DataFrame.

    QA-flow counterpart of the document readers, and the CSV successor of the
    original QA JSON reader (2026-08-19: QA packs are authored as CSV so a
    curator who does not read JSON can open and edit them in Excel/Sheets — a
    spreadsheet is the format at the boundary, everything downstream of this
    component is unchanged). It consumes the 1-row DataFrame emitted by
    APIPipelineInput-tfiG6-QA (which the FastAPI /v1/ingest fills with
    file_path, processing_uuid, file_uuid — see api/app/main.py:372). It
    parses the clean UTF-8 text handed over in-dataframe by
    QaEncodingNormalizer (column `file_content_utf8`), falling back to reading
    `file_path` from disk for standalone/UI runs, and emits one row per QA pair
    while PROPAGATING processing_uuid + file_uuid + file_name onto every row
    (same provenance contract as document_* tables).

    CSV shape: one header row + one data row per QA pair. Delimiter is
    sniffed (';' — Czech Excel's default — or ','), quoting is the standard
    RFC 4180 dialect, so a multi-line answer or a variants cell with one
    phrasing per line just needs to be quoted, which Excel/Sheets does
    automatically the moment a cell holds a newline.
    Header aliases (case-insensitive): question q | question | canonical_q;
    answer a | answer | answer_md; category (optional) cat | category;
    variants (optional, one phrasing per line in the cell) variants |
    phrasings | alt | alt_questions; sources (optional, one source per line,
    `Titulek | URL`) sources | zdroje | asset_refs.

    Output columns: canonical_q, answer_md, category, asset_refs,
                    processing_uuid, file_uuid, file_name.
    """

    display_name = "QA CSV Reader (API row → QA rows)"
    description = "Reads the QA CSV at pipeline file_path into rows, propagating processing_uuid + file_uuid."

    inputs = [
        DataFrameInput(
            name="input_df",
            display_name="API Pipeline DataFrame",
            info="Output of APIPipelineInput — must contain file_path (+ processing_uuid, file_uuid).",
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="file_path_override",
            display_name="File path override (UI testing)",
            info="Optional. If set, used instead of the DataFrame's file_path.",
            required=False,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        # Connectivity for the LANGUAGE REGISTRY only (code_list('language')).
        # This component is the single place where a pack's language is decided,
        # so it is the place that must know which languages the deployment has
        # active and which one is the is_processing_fallback. Env-sourced,
        # hidden, override_skip — same pattern as the lemmatizer components.
        StrInput(name="pg_host", display_name="Postgres Host", show=False, required=False),
        StrInput(name="pg_port", display_name="Postgres Port", show=False, required=False),
        StrInput(name="pg_database", display_name="Postgres Database", show=False, required=False),
        StrInput(name="pg_user", display_name="Postgres User", show=False, required=False),
        SecretStrInput(name="pg_password", display_name="Postgres Password", show=False, required=False),
        StrInput(name="pg_schema", display_name="Postgres Schema", show=False, required=False),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(name="result", display_name="QA DataFrame", method="process", type=DataFrame)
    ]

    def _language_registry(self):
        """{"active": [codes...], "fallback": code|None} from code_list('language').

        code_list('language') WHERE is_active is the single registry of
        languages — adding one starts THERE, never in code, and every consumer
        (search API, web chat, ingestion API) reads it at runtime. `fallback` is
        the row flagged is_processing_fallback, used when the pack's content
        carries no language signal at all. is_ui_default is NOT read: that flag
        only decides what a form preselects and must never pick a reducer.

        NO built-in language pair as a fallback: the language decided here
        selects the reducers for the whole pack and scopes its pack_id,
        thresholds and deactivation — all of it PERSISTED. Guessing the set of
        languages would silently write an index nobody can later identify as
        wrong, whereas a failed ingest is simply re-run. So this raises.
        """
        reg = None
        if not getattr(self, "pg_password", None):
            raise ValueError(
                "no Postgres credentials: the language registry (code_list) "
                "decides this pack's language and must not be guessed — check "
                "the Langflow variables")
        try:
            import psycopg2
            schema = self.pg_schema or "edu_ai"
            conn = psycopg2.connect(host=self.pg_host, port=int(self.pg_port or 5432),
                                    user=self.pg_user, password=self.pg_password,
                                    dbname=self.pg_database)
            try:
                with conn.cursor() as cur:
                    cur.execute(
                        f"SELECT code, is_processing_fallback FROM {schema}.code_list "
                        "WHERE list_code = 'language' AND is_active "
                        "ORDER BY sort_order, code")
                    rows = cur.fetchall()
                if rows:
                    reg = {"active": [r[0] for r in rows],
                           "fallback": next((r[0] for r in rows if r[1]), None)}
                    logger.info(f"[QA-READ] registry from DB: active={reg['active']} "
                                f"fallback={reg['fallback']}")
            finally:
                conn.close()
        except Exception as e:
            raise ValueError(
                f"could not read the language registry code_list('language') "
                f"from Postgres: {e}") from e
        if not reg or not reg.get("active"):
            raise ValueError(
                "code_list('language') has no active row — activate a language "
                "before ingesting")
        return reg

    _Q_KEYS = ("q", "question", "canonical_q")
    _A_KEYS = ("a", "answer", "answer_md")
    _C_KEYS = ("cat", "category")
    # CURATOR-SUPPLIED phrasings (produktový vlastník prepares them, or an AI outside this
    # system does). When present they are AUTHORITATIVE — the LLM variant pass
    # downstream is ignored for that entry, so the pack is reproducible instead
    # of depending on what the model happened to write this time.
    _V_KEYS = ("variants", "phrasings", "alt", "alt_questions")
    # the curator-controlled stable identity (migration 152) and the removal flag
    _K_KEYS = ("entry_key", "key", "klic")
    _ACT_KEYS = ("is_active", "active", "aktivni")
    # CITED SOURCES, one per line in the cell -> qa_entries.asset_refs. Optional:
    # a pack that carries no sources column stores NULL, exactly as before.
    _SRC_KEYS = ("sources", "zdroje", "asset_refs")

    def _read_text(self, path: str) -> str:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
        try:
            return raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            for enc in ("windows-1250", "iso-8859-2"):
                try:
                    return raw.decode(enc)
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    continue
            return raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

    # to-das FAQ export leaves [p]/[/p] pseudo-tags in some answers — strip any
    # such square-bracket paragraph markup so curated answers are stored clean
    _MARKUP_RE = re.compile(r"\[/?p\]")

    @classmethod
    def _pick(cls, d: dict, keys) -> str:
        for k in keys:
            if k in d and d[k] not in (None, ""):
                return cls._MARKUP_RE.sub("", str(d[k])).strip()
        return ""

    @staticmethod
    def _sniff_dialect(sample: str):
        """Excel/RFC 4180 quoting, with only the DELIMITER taken from the file.

        csv.Sniffer is asked for the delimiter and nothing else. Its quoting
        guesses are not trustworthy: it reports doublequote=False unless the
        sample happens to show a "" adjacent to a delimiter, and the field
        `Ředitelka řekla ""ano""` then comes back with the doubling still in it.
        Because the export writes the same doubling, that turns a round-trip into
        CUMULATIVE corruption — each cycle doubles the quotes again. Every real
        producer here (Excel, Sheets, csv.writer, /v1/qa-export) writes RFC 4180,
        so the quoting is fixed and only the delimiter is inferred.
        """
        delim = ";"
        try:
            delim = csv.Sniffer().sniff(sample, delimiters=";,\t").delimiter
        except csv.Error:
            pass          # a single-column file has no delimiter to find

        class _Dialect(csv.excel):
            delimiter = delim

        return _Dialect

    @staticmethod
    def _unclosed_quote_row(text: str):
        """Spreadsheet row holding a double quote that is never closed, or None.

        RFC 4180 doubles a quote inside a quoted field, so a well-formed file
        holds an EVEN number of them — an odd count means one field never
        closes. That case needs its own check because csv then merges the whole
        rest of the file into that one cell: nothing comes out empty and every
        row but one disappears, so neither a per-cell nor a field-count check
        can see it.
        """
        if text.count('"') % 2 == 0:
            return None
        row, opened_at, inside, i, n = 1, 1, False, 0, len(text)
        while i < n:
            c = text[i]
            if c == '"':
                if inside and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '"':
                    i += 2          # an escaped quote inside a quoted field
                    continue
                if not inside:
                    opened_at = row
                inside = not inside
            elif c == "\n" and not inside:
                row += 1            # a line break inside a cell is not a new row
            i += 1
        return opened_at

    def _parse_rows(self, text: str) -> list:
        """[(excel_row, {lowercased header: cell}), ...].

        excel_row is the number the curator sees in the spreadsheet: the header
        is row 1 and a multi-line cell still occupies a single row, so the
        record index maps straight onto it. Every error below names it, because
        that is how a CSV problem gets fixed."""
        # a stray BOM only survives the standalone disk-read fallback —
        # QaEncodingNormalizer already strips it on the API path
        text = text.lstrip("﻿")
        sample = text[:4096]
        if not sample.strip():
            raise ValueError("QA CSV is empty.")
        bad_quote = self._unclosed_quote_row(text)
        if bad_quote is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"row {bad_quote}: a double quote is opened and never closed, so "
                "everything after it reads as ONE cell and the rows below are "
                'lost. A cell holding a quote must double it (""), and a cell '
                "holding the delimiter or a line break must be wrapped in quotes.")
        dialect = self._sniff_dialect(sample)
        reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), dialect=dialect)
        if not reader.fieldnames:
            raise ValueError("QA CSV has no header row.")
        header = [(h or "").strip().lower() for h in reader.fieldnames]
        # Naming what the header DOES hold turns the usual cause — a delimiter
        # the sniffer read differently, so the whole line landed in one column —
        # into something the curator can see and fix.
        for label, keys in (("question", self._Q_KEYS), ("answer", self._A_KEYS)):
            if not any(k in header for k in keys):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"QA CSV header has no {label} column: expected one of "
                    f"{', '.join(keys)}, found {header}")
        out = []
        for i, raw_row in enumerate(reader):
            excel_row = i + 2
            # More values than columns means a delimiter sits unquoted inside a
            # cell. Missing TRAILING values are left alone on purpose — writing
            # `Q;A` for a four-column header is normal hand-editing, and if the
            # gap hits the question or the answer the check below names the row.
            extra = raw_row.get(None)
            if extra:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"row {excel_row}: {len(header) + len(extra)} values for "
                    f"{len(header)} columns — an unquoted "
                    f"{getattr(dialect, 'delimiter', ';')!r} inside a cell? "
                    "A cell containing the delimiter must be wrapped in quotes.")
            item = {(k or "").strip().lower(): (v if v is not None else "")
                    for k, v in raw_row.items() if k is not None}
            out.append((excel_row, item))
        return out

    def process(self) -> DataFrame:
        df_in = self.input_df
        row = {}
        if isinstance(df_in, pd.DataFrame) and not df_in.empty:
            row = df_in.iloc[0].to_dict()

        # Prefer the clean UTF-8 text handed over by QaEncodingNormalizer in the
        # DataFrame (column `file_content_utf8`) — no file read, so no dependency
        # on the shared uploads volume's cross-container write permissions. Fall
        # back to reading `file_path` from disk (standalone / UI runs).
        content = row.get("file_content_utf8")
        if not (isinstance(content, str) and content.strip()):
            content = None

        path = (self.file_path_override or row.get("file_path") or "").strip()
        if content is None and (not path or not os.path.isfile(path)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"QA CSV not available: no in-dataframe content and file not found: {path!r}"
            )

        # provenance from the API row (generate as fallback for standalone/UI runs).
        # Pack metadata (pack_uuid, subject, grade, lang) comes from the API too —
        # exactly like document ingestion — never hardcoded in the insert component.
        processing_uuid = row.get("processing_uuid") or str(uuid.uuid4())
        file_uuid = row.get("file_uuid") or str(uuid.uuid4())
        file_name = row.get("file_name") or (os.path.basename(path) if path else "qa.csv")
        # MD manifest fields — semantic pack_id + schema_version + per-pack thresholds
        schema_version = row.get("schema_version") or 1
        t_answer = row.get("t_answer") if row.get("t_answer") is not None else 0.60
        t_suggest = row.get("t_suggest") if row.get("t_suggest") is not None else 0.30
        m_margin = row.get("m_margin") if row.get("m_margin") is not None else 0.08
        school_subject = row.get("school_subject")
        school_subject_grade = row.get("school_subject_grade")
        # merge (default) = the file says what it touches, rows it does not
        # mention stay as they are. replace = the file IS the pack, anything
        # missing from it is deactivated. The safe one is the default on purpose:
        # the worst a mangled edit can then do is fail to update something.
        qa_mode = (row.get("qa_mode") or "merge").strip().lower()
        if qa_mode not in ("merge", "replace"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"qa_mode must be 'merge' or 'replace', got {qa_mode!r}")

        data = self._parse_rows(content if content is not None else self._read_text(path))

        # LANGUAGE — deterministic, exactly like document ingestion, and resolved
        # ONCE here: the pack's language selects the lemmatizer/stemmer further
        # down (ChunkLemmatizer-qa003 consumes this column) and scopes the
        # pack_id, thresholds and deactivation. Priority: the user's číselník
        # code > shared detect_lang over the pack's own Q+A > the registry's
        # is_processing_fallback. Never a hardcoded "cs" — that used to push an
        # English pack into cs-core and DEACTIVATE the Czech pack.
        _reg = self._language_registry()
        _active, _fallback = _reg["active"], _reg["fallback"]
        document_language = (row.get("document_language") or "").strip().lower() or None
        lang_source = "user"
        if document_language not in _active:
            _sample = " ".join(
                str(it.get(k, ""))
                for _, it in data[:40]
                for k in ("q", "question", "canonical_q", "a", "answer", "answer_md")
            )[:6000]
            document_language = detect_lang(_sample, allowed=tuple(_active))
            lang_source = "detected"
            if not document_language:
                # detect_lang returns None for "cannot tell" and we do not guess:
                # take the registry's fallback and SAY SO in the log, so a pack
                # that landed on it can be corrected by supplying the language.
                document_language = _fallback
                lang_source = "registry-fallback"
                if not document_language:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "pack language undeterminable and code_list('language') has "
                        "no is_processing_fallback row — set one or pass "
                        "document_language on the ingest request")
                logger.warning(
                    f"[QA-READ] no language signal in pack -> registry fallback "
                    f"'{document_language}'")
        lang_detected = lang_source != "user"
        logger.info(f"[QA-READ] pack language={document_language} ({lang_source})")

        # PACK IDENTITY, in priority order:
        #   1. user_defined_pack_id — an explicit curator override; honoured
        #      VERBATIM so two packs can coexist for the same
        #      language-subject-grade triple, or a pack can keep a stable name
        #      independent of its metadata. NOTE: it overrides only the IDENTITY;
        #      manifest `lang` still comes from the resolved language, so the
        #      /search language filter keeps working.
        #   2. pack_id prefilled by the API (only when the user supplied a language)
        #   3. derived language-subject-grade — built HERE, because the language is
        #      only final after detection.
        user_pack = (row.get("user_defined_pack_id") or "").strip()
        if not user_pack:
            raise ValueError(
                "QA pack needs a name: send user_defined_pack_id "
                "(letters, digits, '-' and '_' only, e.g. 'prijimacky'). "
                "Uploading a pack of the SAME name replaces its previous version, "
                "so the name is the replacement key and must be chosen, not guessed.")
        if not _PACK_ID_RX.match(user_pack):
            raise ValueError(
                f"pack_id {user_pack!r} is not allowed: use ASCII letters, digits, "
                "'-' and '_' only (no diacritics, no spaces).")
        pack_id = user_pack
        pack_source = "user_defined"

        logger.info(
            f"[QA READER] language={document_language} "
            f"({'detected' if lang_detected else 'user'}), "
            f"pack_id={pack_id} ({pack_source})")

        rows = []
        taken_keys = set()
        for excel_row, item in data:
            q = self._pick(item, self._Q_KEYS)
            a = self._pick(item, self._A_KEYS)
            # entry_key: the curator's own, or derived from the question. Taken
            # BEFORE the empty-answer check below so a deactivation row need not
            # repeat the answer — see want_active.
            entry_key = self._pick(item, self._K_KEYS)
            if entry_key:
                if entry_key in taken_keys:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"row {excel_row}: entry_key {entry_key!r} appears twice "
                        "in this file — one key is one entry, and the upload "
                        "could not tell which row should win")
                taken_keys.add(entry_key)
            _act = self._pick(item, self._ACT_KEYS).strip().lower()
            if _act in _FALSEISH:
                want_active = False
            elif _act in _TRUEISH:
                want_active = True
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"row {excel_row}: is_active is {_act!r}, which is neither "

                "legal_entity_code": row.get("legal_entity_code"),

                "valid_to": row.get("valid_to"),
                "qa_mode": qa_mode,
            })

        if not rows:
            raise ValueError("QA CSV has a header but no data rows.")

        return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame(rows))

from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.io import DataFrameInput, StrInput, Output
from lfx.schema.dataframe import DataFrame

import re
import json
import uuid
import pandas as pd


class QAVariantExploder(Component):
    """Explodes Batch-Run output into one row per question phrasing.

    Input: the DataFrame produced by Batch Run, where each original QA row has
    a column (default `variants_json`) holding the LLM's alternative phrasings.
    For every original row this component:
      * mints a PROVISIONAL `entry_id` (UUID) shared by the whole entry — it is a
        grouping token that ties an entry's phrasings together through the
        DataFrame, NOT the identity. PostgresInsertQA resolves the real
        entry_id from entry_key (migration 152) and reuses the one already
        stored for that key, so re-uploading a pack no longer renames every
        entry. A key seen for the first time keeps the uuid minted here.
      * emits the canonical question as variant #1 (role='canonical'),
      * parses the LLM column (JSON array preferred; newline fallback) and emits
        one row per alternative phrasing (role='alt_1', 'alt_2', ...).

    The LLM is expected to return a JSON array of strings, optionally wrapped in
    a ```json fenced block. Robust fallbacks handle plain lines / trailing prose.

    Output columns: entry_id, phrasing, role, canonical_q, answer_md, category.
    Feed this into the Chunk Lemmatizer (text_column='phrasing') and then into
    Postgres Insert QA.
    """

    display_name = "QA Variant Exploder (LLM → phrasing rows)"
    description = "Parses Batch-Run alternative questions and explodes to one row per phrasing (+ canonical)."

    inputs = [
        DataFrameInput(name="dataframe", display_name="Batch-Run DataFrame"),
        StrInput(name="variants_column", display_name="Variants column", value="variants_json"),
        StrInput(name="question_column", display_name="Canonical question column", value="canonical_q"),
        StrInput(name="max_variants", display_name="Max alternatives per entry", value="3"),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(name="result", display_name="Exploded variants DataFrame", method="process", type=DataFrame)
    ]

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_text(raw) -> str:
        """Reduce a possibly-structured LLM response to the plain answer text.

        Reasoning models (e.g. gpt-5.x) return content as a list of blocks
        [{type:'reasoning',...}, {type:'text','text':'...'}]; the useful payload
        is the text block(s). Handles the live object and its stringified form.
        """
        import ast
        if isinstance(raw, list):
            texts = [str(b.get("text")) for b in raw
                     if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("text")]
            return "\n".join(texts) if texts else ""
        s = str(raw or "").strip()
        if s.startswith("[") and ("'text'" in s or '"text"' in s):
            try:
                return QAVariantExploder._extract_text(ast.literal_eval(s))
            except Exception:
                m = re.findall(r"['\"]text['\"]\s*:\s*['\"](.+?)['\"]\s*[,}\]]", s, re.DOTALL)
                if m:
                    return "\n".join(m)
        return s

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_variants(raw) -> list:
        s = QAVariantExploder._extract_text(raw)
        if not s:
            return []
        m = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(.+?)```", s, re.DOTALL)
        if m:
            s = m.group(1).strip()
        items = None
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(s)
            if isinstance(parsed, list):
                items = parsed
            elif isinstance(parsed, dict):
                items = parsed.get("variants") or list(parsed.values())
        except Exception:
            items = [re.sub(r'^\s*(?:[-*\d\.\)]+\s*)', '', ln).strip().strip('"')
                     for ln in s.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
        out, seen = [], set()
        for it in (items or []):
            t = str(it).strip().strip('"').strip()
            if not t or t[0] in "{[":       # skip stray structured junk
                continue
            k = t.lower()
            if k not in seen:
                seen.add(k)
                out.append(t)
        return out

    def process(self) -> DataFrame:
        df = self.dataframe
        if not isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame) or df.empty:
            raise ValueError("QAVariantExploder: empty/invalid input DataFrame")

        vcol = self.variants_column or "variants_json"
        qcol = self.question_column or "canonical_q"
        cap = int(self.max_variants or 3)

        rows = []
        for _, r in df.iterrows():
            canonical = str(r.get(qcol, "")).strip()
            if not canonical:
                continue
            eid = str(uuid.uuid4())
            answer = r.get("answer_md", r.get("a", ""))
            category = r.get("category", r.get("cat", ""))

            base = {"entry_id": eid, "canonical_q": canonical,
                    "answer_md": answer, "category": category,
                    # provenance + pack metadata carried from the API row (QA JSON Reader)
                    "processing_uuid": r.get("processing_uuid"),
                    "file_uuid": r.get("file_uuid"),
                    "file_name": r.get("file_name", r.get("source_file", "")),
                    "pack_id": r.get("pack_id"),
                    "schema_version": r.get("schema_version"),
                    "t_answer": r.get("t_answer"),
                    "t_suggest": r.get("t_suggest"),
                    "m_margin": r.get("m_margin"),
                    "school_subject": r.get("school_subject"),
                    "school_subject_grade": r.get("school_subject_grade"),
                    "document_language": r.get("document_language"),
                    "legal_entity_code": r.get("legal_entity_code"),
                    "user_id": r.get("user_id"),
                    "visibility": r.get("visibility"),
                    "audience_roles": r.get("audience_roles"),
                 "document_grade_orig": r.get("document_grade_orig"),
                 "document_domain_orig": r.get("document_domain_orig"),
                 "school_subject": r.get("school_subject"),
                 "valid_from": r.get("valid_from"),
                 "valid_to": r.get("valid_to"),
                    # identity + intent from the CSV row, needed by the upsert in
                    # PostgresInsertQA. entry_key survives rephrasing, which
                    # entry_id above cannot; want_active=False means "switch this
                    # entry off" and qa_mode decides what an ABSENT row means.
                    "asset_refs": r.get("asset_refs"),
                    "entry_key": r.get("entry_key"),
                    "want_active": bool(r.get("want_active", True)),
                    "qa_mode": r.get("qa_mode") or "merge",
                   "variant_source": None}

            # A row that only switches an entry OFF has no phrasings to store:
            # emit it once so the insert sees the intent, and skip the variants.
            if not base["want_active"]:
                rows.append({**base, "phrasing": "", "role": "deactivate",
                             "variant_source": None})
                continue

            # variant #1 = canonical
            rows.append({**base, "phrasing": canonical, "role": "canonical",
                           "variant_source": "canonical"})

            # Phrasings come WITH the entry (QA JSON `variants`) — curated by a
            # human or prepared by an AI OUTSIDE this system (produktový vlastník, 2026-08-18).
            # The LLM generation pass that used to sit upstream was removed with
            # it: a pack is now reproducible (the same file ingests to the same
            # rows) and costs no tokens. An entry that ships no variants simply
            # gets its canonical phrasing — nothing is invented here.
            variants = self._parse_variants(r.get("curated_variants"))
            source = "curated"
            # never let an alternative duplicate the canonical
            variants = [v for v in variants if v.lower() != canonical.lower()]
            # No cap: truncating would silently drop phrasings someone deliberately
            # wrote (five supplied, three stored). `max_variants` guarded a chatty
            # GENERATION, which no longer happens here.
            for i, v in enumerate(variants, 1):
                rows.append({**base, "phrasing": v, "role": f"alt_{i}",
                             "variant_source": source})

        return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame(rows))

from eduai_normalize import normalize_tokens, lemma_tokens, stem_tokens, detect_lang


class ChunkLemmatizer(Component):
    """Adds three PURE Czech fulltext columns (norm / lemma / stem) per chunk.

        chunk_norm_text   surface tokens — lower, diacritics stripped, stopword-free
        chunk_lemma_text  simplemma LEMMAS only (no stemmer)
        chunk_stem_text   Dolamic-Savoy light STEMS only (no lemma)

    Postgres generates ts_norm / ts_lemma / ts_stem over these; the search setting
    picks which form to match. Never mixes stemmer + lemmatizer in one text (per
    produktový vlastník). SHARED contract (module-level above) — keep byte-identical to
    search/app/text_norm.py or query↔index parity breaks. Uses v1-default
    normalization (cfg=None); a non-default profile requires passing its params.
    """

    display_name = "Chunk Lemmatizer (norm + lemma + stem columns)"
    description = (
        "Adds chunk_norm_text (surface), chunk_lemma_text (simplemma lemmas) and "
        "chunk_stem_text (light-stemmer stems) — three pure forms for the tsvectors."
    )

    inputs = [
        DataFrameInput(name="dataframe", display_name="Chunk rows",
                       info="Vector-ready chunk DataFrame (must contain the text column)."),
        StrInput(name="text_column", display_name="Text column", value="chunk_text"),
        StrInput(name="norm_column", display_name="Output: normalized surface column",
                 value="chunk_norm_text", advanced=True),
        StrInput(name="lemma_column", display_name="Output: lemma column",
                 value="chunk_lemma_text", advanced=True),
        StrInput(name="stem_column", display_name="Output: stem column",
                 value="chunk_stem_text", advanced=True),
        # which ingest context this run is — engines[].active[context] decides
        # whether the lemma / stem column is populated ("ingest_qa" | "ingest_docs").
        StrInput(name="context", display_name="Ingest context",
                 value="ingest_qa", advanced=True),
        # optional DB access to load the qa_stopword číselník (data, not code).
        # If password is unset, the in-code STOPWORDS fallback is used.
        StrInput(name="pg_host", display_name="Postgres Host", value="edu_ai_postgres", advanced=True),
        StrInput(name="pg_port", display_name="Postgres Port", value="5432", advanced=True),
        StrInput(name="pg_user", display_name="Postgres User", value="edu_ai", advanced=True),
        SecretStrInput(name="pg_password", display_name="Postgres Password", required=False, advanced=True),
        StrInput(name="pg_database", display_name="Postgres Database", value="edu_ai", advanced=True),
        StrInput(name="pg_schema", display_name="Postgres Schema", value="edu_ai", advanced=True),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(name="result", display_name="DataFrame + norm/lemma/stem", method="process", type=DataFrame),
    ]

    def _load_ctx(self):
        """From the active settings + qa_stopword table, return
        (cfg, emit_lemma, emit_stem) for this ingest context. Without DB access:
        (None, True, True) — built-in stopwords, all forms computed.
        """
        ctx = (self.context or "ingest_qa").strip()
        if not getattr(self, "pg_password", None):
            return None, True, True
        cfg, emit_lemma, emit_stem = None, True, True
        try:
            import psycopg2
            schema = self.pg_schema or "edu_ai"
            conn = psycopg2.connect(host=self.pg_host, port=int(self.pg_port or 5432),
                                    user=self.pg_user, password=self.pg_password, dbname=self.pg_database)
            try:
                with conn.cursor() as cur:
                    cur.execute(f"SELECT lang, term FROM {schema}.qa_stopword WHERE is_active")
                    by_lang = {}
                    for _lang, _term in cur.fetchall():
                        by_lang.setdefault(_lang, []).append(_term)
                    if by_lang:
                        # No legacy flat `stopwords` key: it was the CZECH list by
                        # construction, making Czech the one language served from a
                        # differently-shaped key (eduai_normalize 1.4.0 reads
                        # stopwords_by_lang only).
                        cfg = {"normalization": {"stopwords_by_lang": by_lang}}
                    cur.execute(f"SELECT config->'engines' FROM {schema}.settings WHERE is_active LIMIT 1")
                    row = cur.fetchone()
                    engines = row[0] if row and row[0] else []

                    def _on(kind):
                        for e in engines:
                            if e.get("kind") == kind:
                                a = e.get("active", True)
                                return bool(a.get(ctx, True)) if isinstance(a, dict) else bool(a)
                        return True
                    emit_lemma, emit_stem = _on("lemmatizer"), _on("stemmer")
                    # engines go INTO cfg: which reducer implements which language
                    # is data (settings.config.engines), and the library
                    # resolves it from cfg — exactly as it does on the query side,
                    # which is what keeps index and query on the same reducer.
                    if engines:
                        cfg = cfg or {}
                        cfg["engines"] = engines
            finally:
                conn.close()
            logger.info(f"[LEMMA] ctx={ctx}: emit lemma={emit_lemma} stem={emit_stem}, "
                        f"{len((cfg or {}).get('normalization', {}).get('stopwords', []))} stopwords")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"[LEMMA] ctx load failed ({e}) — built-in stopwords, all forms")
        return cfg, emit_lemma, emit_stem

    def process(self) -> DataFrame:
        df = self.dataframe
        if not isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame) or df.empty:
            logger.warning("[LEMMA] empty/invalid input")
            return DataFrame(df if isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame) else pd.DataFrame())

        tcol = (self.text_column or "chunk_text").strip()
        ncol = (self.norm_column or "chunk_norm_text").strip()
        lcol = (self.lemma_column or "chunk_lemma_text").strip()
        scol = (self.stem_column or "chunk_stem_text").strip()

        if tcol not in df.columns:
            logger.error(f"[LEMMA] column '{tcol}' missing (have: {list(df.columns)})")
            return DataFrame(df.copy())

        # stoplist from qa_stopword (data) + which forms this ingest context wants
        cfg, emit_lemma, emit_stem = self._load_ctx()

        # LANGUAGE — consumed, not decided. QAJsonReader already resolved it for
        # the whole pack (user code > detect_lang > registry fallback) and put it
        # in `document_language`; a pack is deliberately single-language, so its
        # identity, thresholds and reducers must all agree. Deciding again here
        # could disagree with the pack_id the reader derived — the reader has the
        # registry and the full Q+A sample, this component has neither.
        lang = None
        if "document_language" in df.columns:
            _lv = df["document_language"].dropna()
            if len(_lv) and str(_lv.iloc[0]).strip():
                lang = str(_lv.iloc[0]).strip().lower()
        if not lang:
            # Only reachable if the flow is rewired so the reader's column is
            # lost. Failing loudly beats reducing the whole pack with a guessed
            # language and silently breaking index↔query parity.
            raise ValueError(
                "document_language missing — QAJsonReader must resolve the pack "
                "language before reduction (do not guess it here)")
        logger.info(f"[LEMMA] language={lang} (from pack, resolved by QAJsonReader)")

        norms, lemmas, stems = [], [], []
        for val in df[tcol]:
            if not isinstance(val, str) or not val.strip():
                norms.append("")
                lemmas.append("")
                stems.append("")
                continue
            norms.append(" ".join(normalize_tokens(val, cfg, lang)))
            if emit_lemma:
                try:
                    lemmas.append(" ".join(lemma_tokens(val, cfg, lang)))
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.error(f"[LEMMA] lemmatization failed: {e}")
                    lemmas.append(" ".join(normalize_tokens(val, cfg, lang)))
            else:
                lemmas.append("")
            stems.append(" ".join(stem_tokens(val, cfg, lang)) if emit_stem else "")

        result = df.copy()
        result[ncol] = norms
        result[lcol] = lemmas
        result[scol] = stems
        logger.info(f"[LEMMA] {len(result)} rows -> {ncol}/{lcol}/{scol} (pure forms, stopword-free)")
        return DataFrame(result)

class PostgresInsertQA(Component):
    """Inserts an exploded QA DataFrame into the qa_* tables (pack schema §2.1).

    QA-flow counterpart of PostgresInsertVectorisedDocuments — same psycopg2 /
    execute_batch pattern, different target: it fills qa_pack_manifest,
    qa_entries and qa_variants instead of document_chunks. No embeddings
    (deterministic lexical pack); the ts_norm/ts_lemma/ts_stem tsvector columns
    are GENERATED by Postgres from the three pure form columns, never inserted here.

    Expected input columns (one row per phrasing, from QA Variant Exploder →
    Chunk Lemmatizer): entry_id, canonical_q, answer_md, category, phrasing,
    plus the three PURE form columns (defaults norm_text / lemma_text / stem_text).
    Rows are tagged with setting_id (which normalization profile produced them).

    Versioning is an UPSERT keyed on entry_key (migration 152), not a wholesale
    replace. An entry whose key is already active is UPDATED IN PLACE, so its
    entry_id survives — question_answer_log.matched_entry_id and the mobile
    pack's PRIMARY KEY both refer to it, and minting a new one per upload made
    both meaningless across versions. A key not seen before is inserted.

    What an ABSENT row means is qa_mode:
      merge (default) — nothing. The file says only what it touches, so a
                        mangled edit fails to update something instead of
                        destroying it.
      replace         — the file IS the pack; active entries it does not name
                        are deactivated.
    A row carrying is_active=FALSE deactivates that entry either way, which is
    how a deletion is stated explicitly rather than by omission.

    Variants are rewritten wholesale for every entry being written (see the
    comment at that step for why they are not diffed). Deactivation always
    cascades to qa_variants AND qa_embedding, because both scan surfaces index
    on is_active — partial ts_*/trgm indexes since migration 149, partial HNSW
    from the start. Old rows are kept for history.

    The pack manifest stays soft-versioned: previous rows are deactivated and the
    new one inserted as the single active row, version auto-incrementing per
    (legal_entity_code, pack_id).
    """

    display_name = "Postgres Insert QA (manifest/entries/variants)"
    description = "Fills qa_pack_manifest, qa_entries and qa_variants from an exploded+lemmatized QA DataFrame."

    inputs = [
        DataFrameInput(name="dataframe", display_name="Exploded + lemmatized QA DataFrame"),

        StrInput(name="pg_host", display_name="Postgres Host", value="edu_ai_postgres"),
        StrInput(name="pg_port", display_name="Postgres Port", value="5432"),
        StrInput(name="pg_user", display_name="Postgres User", value="edu_ai"),
        SecretStrInput(name="pg_password", display_name="Postgres Password", required=True),
        StrInput(name="pg_database", display_name="Postgres Database", value="edu_ai"),
        StrInput(name="pg_schema", display_name="Postgres Schema", value="edu_ai"),
    ]

    # Pure persistence — NO pack metadata inputs. pack_uuid / subject / grade /
    # lang all arrive on the DataFrame rows (propagated from the API pipeline_input
    # via QA JSON Reader → Variant Exploder), exactly like document ingestion.
    # Fixed-contract constants: ChunkLemmatizer's output columns are invariant.
    # A/B/C thresholds are per-pack (MD §2.4) and arrive on the rows from the API.
    NORM_COL, LEMMA_COL, STEM_COL = "norm_text", "lemma_text", "stem_text"

    outputs = [
        Output(name="result", display_name="Insert Result", method="process", type=DataFrame)
    ]

    DB_BATCH_SIZE = 200

    def process(self) -> DataFrame:
        name = self.__class__.__name__
        df = self.dataframe
        if not isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame) or df.empty:
            return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame([{"component_name": name, "result": "empty/invalid input"}]))

        ncol, lcol, scol = self.NORM_COL, self.LEMMA_COL, self.STEM_COL
        required = ["entry_id", "canonical_q", "answer_md", "phrasing", ncol, lcol, scol]
        missing = [c for c in required if c not in df.columns]
        if missing:
            return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame([{"component_name": name, "result": f"Missing columns: {missing}"}]))

        schema = self.pg_schema or "edu_ai"
        # pack metadata from the API (first row) — mirrors document ingestion
        meta = df.iloc[0].to_dict()
        # MD manifest fields, entered via the API and propagated on the rows
        # no fallback name: the reader refuses an upload without one, and a
        # default here would resurrect the very collision that removal fixed
        pack = (meta.get("pack_id") or "").strip()
        if not pack:
            return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame([{"component_name": name,
                "result": "ERROR: missing pack_id (user_defined_pack_id is required)"}]))
        # WHOSE pack this is, WHO imported it, HOW FAR it reaches — every qa_*
        # row carries them, so retrieval never has to join to find out.
        legal_entity_code = meta.get("legal_entity_code")
        owner_user_id = meta.get("user_id")
        visibility = meta.get("visibility") or "entity"
        _ar = meta.get("audience_roles")
        if isinstance(_ar, str) and _ar.strip():
            try:
                import json as _qj
                _ar = _qj.loads(_ar)
            except Exception:
                _ar = None
        audience_roles = list(_ar) if isinstance(_ar, (list, tuple)) and len(_ar) else None
        # the ingest API's single předmět — still the SOURCE of school_subject_ids
        # below, but no longer a manifest column of its own (dropped in 145: only
        # the id array remains, because only it can hold SEVERAL values). "core"
        # survives purely as the sentinel for "no předmět declared".
        subject = meta.get("school_subject") or "core"
        lang = meta.get("document_language")   # resolved in QAJsonReader (user > detect_lang);
        # "cs" here would silently mislabel an English pack
        # likewise the single ročník: only a FALLBACK feeding grade_codes when the
        # caller sent no multi-value list (below). The scalar column went with 145.
        _g = meta.get("school_subject_grade")
        grade = int(_g) if str(_g).strip().isdigit() else None
        # DECLARED SETS from the ingest API (migration 140). The gateway has always
        # sent these — the QA flow only ever read the single school_subject_grade,
        # which is why a pack could not be multi-grade, domain-tagged or SŠ. Same
        # JSON-string carriers the document branches use.
        def _json_list(v):
            if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
                return [str(x) for x in v if str(x).strip()]
            if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
                try:
                    import json as _j
                    d = _j.loads(v)
                    return [str(x) for x in d if str(x).strip()] if isinstance(d, list) else []
                except Exception:
                    return []
            return []

        grade_codes = _json_list(meta.get("document_grade_orig"))
        if not grade_codes and grade is not None:
            grade_codes = [str(grade)]          # single-grade uploads still work
        domain_codes = _json_list(meta.get("document_domain_orig"))
        subject_codes = [subject] if subject and subject != "core" else []
        _vf = meta.get("valid_from") or None
        _vt = meta.get("valid_to") or None
        valid_from = str(_vf)[:10] if _vf else None
        valid_to = str(_vt)[:10] if _vt else None
        schema_version = int(meta.get("schema_version") or 1)
        t_answer = float(meta["t_answer"]) if meta.get("t_answer") is not None else 0.60
        t_suggest = float(meta["t_suggest"]) if meta.get("t_suggest") is not None else 0.30
        m_margin = float(meta["m_margin"]) if meta.get("m_margin") is not None else 0.08
        # one timezone-aware timestamp for the whole ingest → identical created_at
        # on every entry + variant of this upload (timestamptz, matching built_at /
        # qa_embedding.created_at). psycopg2 adapts an aware datetime to timestamptz.
        ingest_ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        # merge (default) = the file says only what it touches; replace = the file
        # IS the pack. Read from the first row like every other pack-level field
        # here; the reader already validated it.
        qa_mode = (meta.get("qa_mode") or "merge").strip().lower()
        if qa_mode not in ("merge", "replace"):
            return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame([{"component_name": name,
                "result": f"ERROR: qa_mode must be merge|replace, got {qa_mode!r}"}]))

        # collapse to distinct entries (canonical row carries display data).
        # The dict key is the exploder's PROVISIONAL entry_id — a grouping token
        # for this upload only. The real entry_id is resolved from entry_key below.
        def _refs(v):
            """The reader's JSON string -> a jsonb value psycopg2 will store as
            an ARRAY. Passing the str straight through would store a quoted
            scalar, which the search side then reads back as not-a-list."""
            if v in (None, ""):
                return None
            try:
                return Json(json.loads(v) if isinstance(v, str) else v)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None

        entries = {}
        for _, r in df.iterrows():
            eid = str(r["entry_id"])
            if eid not in entries:
                entries[eid] = {
                    "entry_key": (str(r.get("entry_key") or "").strip() or None),
                    "want_active": bool(r.get("want_active", True)),
                    "canonical_q": str(r["canonical_q"]),
                    "answer_md": str(r["answer_md"]),
                    # curator metadata only. The old "source" key held the
                    # uploaded file's name, which file_uuid on this very row
                    # already identifies — a second copy nothing could keep in
                    # step (dropped in 146). category comes from the pack JSON
                    # ("cat"/"category") and is read by the device-pack export.
                    "tags": {"category": r.get("category", "")},
                    # curator-cited sources, already JSON from the reader
                    "asset_refs": r.get("asset_refs") or None,
                    "processing_uuid": r.get("processing_uuid") or None,
                    "file_uuid": r.get("file_uuid") or None,
                }

        conn = cur = None
        try:
            conn = psycopg2.connect(host=self.pg_host, port=int(self.pg_port), user=self.pg_user,
                                    password=self.pg_password, dbname=self.pg_database)
            conn.autocommit = False
            cur = conn.cursor()

            # PROSPECTIVE ingest: stamp rows with whatever setting is active NOW.
            # A later setting change (e.g. stemmer light→hard) does NOT touch this
            # batch — it applies only to the next ingest, which stamps the new id.
            cur.execute(f"SELECT setting_id FROM {schema}.settings WHERE is_active LIMIT 1")
            _sr = cur.fetchone()
            setting_id = _sr[0] if _sr else None

            # ── ročník/subject/domain CODES -> entity-resolved IDS (migration 140)
            # A ročník is a ROW of THAT unit's číselník: SOŠ owns 10..13, a ZŠ 1..9.
            # entity_grade_scope() = the entity's subtree UNION what resolves upwards,
            # because an umbrella org's own codebook holds just 9999 while its units
            # carry the numbers. DISTINCT ON prefers the entity's OWN row when several
            # units share a code (9999 exists once per unit).
            cur.execute(
                f"SELECT DISTINCT ON (t.code) t.id, t.code FROM ("
                f"  SELECT c.id, c.code, (c.legal_entity_code = %s) AS own"
                f"    FROM {schema}.entity_grade_scope(%s) s"
                f"    JOIN {schema}.code_list c ON c.id = s.id) t"
                f" ORDER BY t.code, t.own DESC",
                (legal_entity_code, legal_entity_code))
            _grade2id = {c: i for i, c in cur.fetchall()}
            school_grade_ids = [_grade2id[c] for c in grade_codes if c in _grade2id] or None

            cur.execute(
                f"SELECT id, code FROM {schema}.resolved_code_list(%s, 'school_subject')",
                (legal_entity_code,))
            _subj2id = {c: i for i, c in cur.fetchall()}
            school_subject_ids = [_subj2id[c] for c in subject_codes if c in _subj2id] or None

            cur.execute(
                f"SELECT id, type_code FROM {schema}.resolved_taxonomy_rules(%s, 'DOMAIN')",
                (legal_entity_code,))
            _dom2id = {c: i for i, c in cur.fetchall()}
            domain_ids = [_dom2id[c] for c in domain_codes if c in _dom2id] or None

            # LEVEL COMES FROM THE INSTITUTION the pack is uploaded under
            # (Martin, 2026-08-18) — legal_entity.level, the same source
            # answer.py calls authoritative for the caller. A pack is metadata of
            # ONE school about one topic, so unlike a document it cannot span ZŠ
            # and SŠ; the unit therefore settles it, whatever ročníky it carries.
            # Deriving from ročníky instead left a "všechny ročníky" (9999) pack
            # of a ZŠ unit with NO level, although the unit is unambiguously ZŠ.
            # The umbrella ORGANISATION has no level of its own and keeps NULL:
            # its pack may serve both units, and the ročník filter still applies.
            cur.execute(f"SELECT level FROM {schema}.legal_entity WHERE legal_entity_code = %s",
                        (legal_entity_code,))
            _lv_row = cur.fetchone()
            school_level = (_lv_row[0] if _lv_row and _lv_row[0] in ("MS", "ZS", "SS") else None)

            # ── BINDING (migration 144) ──────────────────────────────────────
            # Its sibling owning_entity_code was dropped in 145: a pack takes its
            # level from the uploading institution, so the derived owner could only
            # be that same institution or NULL — legal_entity_code already says it.
            # The binding survives because it is NOT derivable from the entity: it
            # comes from domain x level x ročník set.
            # Same rule as _derive_binding() in the document metadata inserter:
            # the binding's level matches (or is NULL = any), ONE declared domain
            # equals the binding's domain, and the declared ročník SET equals the
            # binding's grade set. More than one match, or none, means no binding
            # — a wrong binding is worse than none, since it carries the authority
            # ladder. Unlike documents there is no grade TRIM here: a pack has no
            # per-chunk grades to whitelist, its ročníky ARE the declaration.
            binding_id = None
            try:
                cur.execute(f"SELECT id, domain_code, school_level, grades "
                            f"FROM {schema}.taxonomy_binding WHERE is_active")
                _decl = {str(g) for g in grade_codes}
                _eff = set(domain_codes or [])
                _uniq = set()
                for _bid, _dcode, _blevel, _bgrades in cur.fetchall():
                    if (_blevel is None or _blevel == school_level) and _dcode in _eff \
                       and {str(g) for g in (_bgrades or [])} == _decl:
                        _uniq.add(_bid)
                binding_id = next(iter(_uniq)) if len(_uniq) == 1 else None
            except Exception as _be:
                conn.rollback()
                binding_id = None
                print(f"[QA] binding derivation failed ({_be}) — pack stored without binding")

            # IDENTITY (migration 152). entry_id used to be minted per upload, so
            # the same content changed id every time — which broke
            # question_answer_log.matched_entry_id across versions and made every
            # entry look new to the mobile pack. entry_key is the curator's stable
            # name for the entry; the id already stored for it is REUSED.
            cur.execute(
                f"SELECT entry_key, entry_id FROM {schema}.qa_entries "
                f"WHERE pack_id = %s AND legal_entity_code = %s AND is_active "
                f"  AND entry_key IS NOT NULL",
                (pack, legal_entity_code))
            known = {r[0]: str(r[1]) for r in cur.fetchall()}

            id_of = {}                     # exploder token -> real entry_id
            to_insert, to_update, off_ids = [], [], []
            noop_off = 0
            for token, e in entries.items():
                key = e["entry_key"]
                eid = known.get(key) or token
                id_of[token] = eid
                if not e["want_active"]:
                    # switching OFF something that is not there is a no-op, not an
                    # error: a curator re-uploading a file that still carries an
                    # old FALSE row means no harm by it.
                    if key in known:
                        off_ids.append(eid)
                    else:
                        noop_off += 1
                elif key in known:
                    to_update.append((eid, e))
                else:
                    to_insert.append((eid, e))

            # REPLACE only: an active entry the file does not mention is dropped.
            # In MERGE it is left alone — that is the whole point, and why merge is
            # the default: a mangled edit then fails to update something instead of
            # destroying it.
            absent_ids = []
            if qa_mode == "replace":
                present = [e["entry_key"] for e in entries.values()
                           if e["want_active"] and e["entry_key"]]
                cur.execute(
                    f"SELECT entry_id FROM {schema}.qa_entries "
                    f"WHERE is_active AND pack_id = %s AND legal_entity_code = %s "
                    # a legacy row with no key cannot be named by the file, so
                    # replace has to drop it too or it would be immortal
                    f"  AND (entry_key IS NULL OR NOT (entry_key = ANY(%s)))",
                    (pack, legal_entity_code, present or [""]))
                absent_ids = [str(r[0]) for r in cur.fetchall()]

            # DEACTIVATION in all three tables carrying the flag. qa_variants and
            # qa_embedding both need it: the lexical indexes are partial on
            # is_active (migration 149) and the HNSW one always was, so a row left
            # active stays matchable.
            gone = sorted(set(off_ids) | set(absent_ids))
            if gone:
                for tbl in ("qa_entries", "qa_variants", "qa_embedding"):
                    cur.execute(f"UPDATE {schema}.{tbl} SET is_active = false "
                                f"WHERE is_active AND entry_id = ANY(%s::uuid[])", (gone,))

            if to_insert:
                execute_batch(cur,
                              f"INSERT INTO {schema}.qa_entries "
                              f"(entry_id, pack_id, entry_key, canonical_q, answer_md, tags, "
                              f" asset_refs, "
                              f" processing_uuid, file_uuid, is_active, created_at, "
                              f" legal_entity_code, owner_user_id, visibility, audience_roles, "
                              f" school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids, domain_ids, "
                              f" binding_id, valid_from, valid_to) "
                              f"VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s, true, %s, %s,%s,%s,%s, %s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)",
                              [(eid, pack, e["entry_key"], e["canonical_q"], e["answer_md"],
                                Json(e["tags"]), _refs(e["asset_refs"]),
                                e["processing_uuid"], e["file_uuid"], ingest_ts,
                                legal_entity_code, owner_user_id, visibility, audience_roles,
                                school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids, domain_ids,
                                binding_id, valid_from, valid_to)
                               for eid, e in to_insert],
                              page_size=self.DB_BATCH_SIZE)

            # An existing entry is UPDATED IN PLACE rather than replaced, so its
            # entry_id — the thing the log and the device refer to — survives. The
            # scope columns are rewritten too: they are denormalised onto every QA
            # table (migration 144), and a changed visibility that landed only on
            # the entry would leave the scan surfaces filtering on the old one.
            if to_update:
                execute_batch(cur,
                              f"UPDATE {schema}.qa_entries SET "
                              f" canonical_q = %s, answer_md = %s, tags = %s, "
                              f" asset_refs = %s, "
                              f" processing_uuid = %s, file_uuid = %s, created_at = %s, "
                              f" owner_user_id = %s, visibility = %s, audience_roles = %s, "
                              f" school_grade_ids = %s, school_level = %s, "
                              f" school_subject_ids = %s, domain_ids = %s, binding_id = %s, "
                              f" valid_from = %s, valid_to = %s, is_active = true "
                              f"WHERE entry_id = %s",
                              [(e["canonical_q"], e["answer_md"], Json(e["tags"]),
                                _refs(e["asset_refs"]),
                                e["processing_uuid"], e["file_uuid"], ingest_ts,
                                owner_user_id, visibility, audience_roles,
                                school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids,
                                domain_ids, binding_id, valid_from, valid_to, eid)
                               for eid, e in to_update],
                              page_size=self.DB_BATCH_SIZE)

            # VARIANTS are rewritten wholesale for every entry being written, not
            # diffed phrasing-by-phrasing. A kept variant row would need its
            # denormalised scope updated (migration 144) while its qa_embedding row
            # still holds a vector of the OLD phrasing unless that is cleared too —
            # two couplings that are easy to get subtly wrong. Rewriting costs the
            # embeddings of one pack and has no such window. (Reusing unchanged
            # vectors is worth doing later, on real data, as its own change.)
            live_ids = [eid for eid, _ in to_insert] + [eid for eid, _ in to_update]
            if live_ids:
                for tbl in ("qa_variants", "qa_embedding"):
                    cur.execute(f"UPDATE {schema}.{tbl} SET is_active = false "
                                f"WHERE is_active AND entry_id = ANY(%s::uuid[])", (live_ids,))

            live = set(live_ids)
            var_rows = [(id_of[str(r["entry_id"])], str(r["phrasing"]),
                         str(r[ncol]), str(r[lcol]), str(r[scol]), setting_id,
                         r.get("processing_uuid") or None, r.get("file_uuid") or None, ingest_ts,
                         legal_entity_code, owner_user_id, visibility, audience_roles,
                         school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids, domain_ids,
                         binding_id, valid_from, valid_to)
                        for _, r in df.iterrows()
                        if str(r.get("phrasing", "")).strip()
                        and id_of.get(str(r["entry_id"])) in live]
            if var_rows:
                execute_batch(cur,
                              f"INSERT INTO {schema}.qa_variants "
                              f"(entry_id, phrasing, norm_text, lemma_text, stem_text, setting_id, "
                              f" processing_uuid, file_uuid, created_at, "
                              f" legal_entity_code, owner_user_id, visibility, audience_roles, "
                              f" school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids, domain_ids, "
                              f" binding_id, valid_from, valid_to) "
                              f"VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s, %s,%s,%s,%s, %s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)",
                              var_rows, page_size=self.DB_BATCH_SIZE)

            # MANIFEST: one active row per (entity, pack), history kept.
            cur.execute(f"UPDATE {schema}.qa_pack_manifest SET is_active = false "
                        f"WHERE is_active AND pack_id = %s AND legal_entity_code = %s",
                        (pack, legal_entity_code))
            cur.execute(
                f"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 FROM {schema}.qa_pack_manifest "
                f"WHERE pack_id = %s AND legal_entity_code = %s",
                (pack, legal_entity_code))
            next_version = cur.fetchone()[0]
            # entry_count is what the pack HOLDS after this upload, not what the
            # file carried — in merge mode those differ, and the manifest number is
            # the one a curator compares against the download.
            cur.execute(
                f"SELECT count(*) FROM {schema}.qa_entries "
                f"WHERE pack_id = %s AND legal_entity_code = %s AND is_active",
                (pack, legal_entity_code))
            active_count = cur.fetchone()[0]
            cur.execute(
                f"INSERT INTO {schema}.qa_pack_manifest "
                f"(pack_id, lang, version, schema_version, processing_uuid, file_uuid, entry_count, "
                f" t_answer, t_suggest, m_margin, built_at, is_active, "
                f" legal_entity_code, owner_user_id, visibility, "
                f" school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids, domain_ids, "
                f" binding_id, "
                f" audience_roles, valid_from, valid_to) "
                f"VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s, true, %s,%s,%s, %s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)",
                (pack, lang, next_version, schema_version,
                 meta.get("processing_uuid") or None, meta.get("file_uuid") or None,
                 active_count,
                 t_answer, t_suggest, m_margin, ingest_ts,
                 legal_entity_code, owner_user_id, visibility,
                 school_grade_ids, school_level, school_subject_ids, domain_ids,
                 binding_id,
                 audience_roles, valid_from, valid_to),
            )

            # What actually happened, in terms a curator can check against the file
            # they uploaded. There is no dry-run preview yet, so this report is the
            # only place the effect of MERGE is visible — `untouched` above all,
            # being the entries the file never mentioned.
            untouched = active_count - len(to_insert) - len(to_update)
            summary = (f"pack '{pack}' v{next_version} [{qa_mode}]: "
                       f"added {len(to_insert)}, updated {len(to_update)}, "
                       f"deactivated {len(gone)}, untouched {untouched}, "
                       f"variants {len(var_rows)}, active entries {active_count}")
            if noop_off:
                summary += f", {noop_off} FALSE row(s) matched nothing"

            # ingestion audit trail (edu_ai.ingestion_log)
            cur.execute(
                f"INSERT INTO {schema}.ingestion_log "
                f"(log_timestamp, processing_uuid, file_uuid, file_name, log_level, "
                f" component_name, log_message, legal_entity_code, user_id) "
                f"VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)",
                (ingest_ts, meta.get("processing_uuid"), meta.get("file_uuid"),
                 meta.get("file_name"), "INFO", name,
                 f"{summary}, setting {setting_id}",
                 legal_entity_code, owner_user_id),
            )

            conn.commit()
            return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame([{
                "component_name": name,
                "stage": "qa_tables",
                "processing_uuid": str(meta.get("processing_uuid") or "") or None,
                "result": f"SUCCESS — {summary}",
            }]))
        except Exception as e:
            if conn:
                conn.rollback()
            return DataFrame(pd.DataFrame([{"component_name": name, "stage": "qa_tables",
                                            "processing_uuid": None,
                                            "result": f"ERROR: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"}]))
        finally:
            if cur:
                cur.close()
            if conn:
                conn.close()
